posts.cooked: The more cards you look at before you decide what to keep, the stronger the power. Imagine a power that said "Draw up to 40 cards. Discard X cards where X is the number of cards drawn minus 1." It's still only gaining you one card in hand, but it effectively lets you search your deck for as many cards of your choice as you have in hand plus the one extra. This is an extreme example, but it illustrates the principle that it is indeed more powerful to look at more cards even if you don't get to keep any more. It increases your flexibility, helps you get to the cards you want faster, and helps you respond to changing threats more efficiently. In a game like Sentinels where it doesn't hurt you to deck out, "Draw 3 Discard 2" is strictly better than "Draw 2 Discard 1" or "Draw 1."
